fields.product: cobalt hydroxide (in hydroxides/concentrates) with copper cathode

rows.notes: Glencore FY2025 production report p.10: KCC cobalt (contained in concentrates and hydroxides) 22.9 kt in 2025 vs 27.2 kt in 2024 (-16%); H2 weaker because Glencore prioritised copper over cobalt under DRC export restrictions. Capacity for cobalt not disclosed. DRC export quota (cobalt, kt): KCC 16.1 for 2026 (incl. 2025 carryover) and 13.3 for 2027 (S5 p.2); output above quota is stored in-country. Ownership split (Glencore/Gecamines) not evidenced here. Table was read from the rendered PDF page (image), not extracted text.

fields.product: cobalt hydroxide (in hydroxides/concentrates) with copper cathode

rows.notes: Glencore FY2025 production report p.10: Mutanda cobalt 10.6 kt in 2025 vs 7.9 kt in 2024 (+34%); Q4 2025 1.8 kt (down sharply). Report attributes H1 2025 growth to higher grades and volumes at Mutanda. Quota (kt Co): 6.7 for 2026 incl. carryover, 5.5 for 2027 (S5). Glencore total DRC cobalt = KCC 22.9 + Mutanda 10.6 = 33.5 kt (production report p.10 'Total Cobalt').

ERG Metalkol page: Kolwezi, Lualaba; nameplate ~100 ktpa copper cathode and ~23 ktpa cobalt in hydroxide; 90% ERG / 10% DRC State; processes historic tailings (Musonoi River valley, Kingamyambo). capacity_ref_year left null (page undated). Production 2025: Reuters/SMM (S7, confirmed quote) says ERG cut cobalt hydroxide output 70% to 5,700 t in 2025 from 19,000 t in 2024 - an ERG-level statement that does not name Metalkol; ERG's Performance Report snippet (S33, reported) attributes 5.7 kt Co to Metalkol. Treat as Metalkol with caution. ERG 2026 DRC export quota 12,325 t (incl. Q4-2025 carryover). ERG's other DRC cobalt assets (Boss Mining, Frontier; Chambishi Metals in Zambia) exist per ERG menu but no data found - not added. [lead] capacity_ref_year = access-year (source undated) fallback.

Mining Technology analyst comment (GlobalData): Musonoi owned Jinchuan 75% / Gecamines 25% (stated in the fetched page summary, not in the short quote), capacity ~7,400 t Co, underground operations began Sept 2025 (search snippets elsewhere say commercial production Nov 2025). start_year 2025 and capacity_ref_year 2026 (publication year fallback) are inferred from that. Production: Jinchuan Intl group cobalt (Ruashi + Musonoi) 2025 = 1,085 t per a secondary summary (S13, reported) and 71 t in 9M 2025 (S12); H1 2026 Musonoi cobalt 4,101 t per search snippet only (not opened). Per-mine 2025 cobalt output not allocated.

fields.product: cobalt metal / cobalt products with cathode copper

rows.notes: CNMC page (dated 2025-05 from URL): Deziwa described as CNMC's largest standalone overseas copper-cobalt investment, 80,000 t cathode copper and 8,000 t cobalt metal annually; capacity_ref_year 2025 is the publication-year fallback. Mining Technology (S9): Kalongwe, Deziwa and Etoile COLLECTIVELY produced 20,430 t Co in 2025; Deziwa closure slated 2030 - per-mine output not given, not allocated. Relationship between Deziwa and Huayou's CDM (existing row huayou-cdm-congo-dongfang-drc) is NOT established by the sources; lead to check for double-counting.

Reuters/Kitco (Apr 2026): the Lubumbashi operation was Chemaf's only producing site, to be suspended for up to two months for maintenance; new owners (Virtus-Lloyds JV, bought mines Mar 2026 for $30m, ~$900m debt assumed) aim for full production at Lubumbashi and Kolwezi by Jan 2027; a July 2026 Semafor snippet says it remained shut. Hence project_state paused. Site name 'Etoile' is from search snippets (Etoile is near Lubumbashi); the Kitco page itself does not name it. Capacity 4,000 t Co hydroxide (25,000 t Cu cathode) from a Spanish-language report snippet only (reported). No output figure found. Part of the 20,430 t Kalongwe/Deziwa/Etoile 2025 combined figure (S9).

Kitco/Reuters: Mutoshi (near Kolwezi) has been stalled since 2019 when processing was suspended; new owners intend to complete the Mutoshi projects, no date. Design capacity 16,000 t Co / 50,000 t Cu per year from a search-result summary of Mining.com only (reported, not opened). Status under_construction/paused is a judgment: plant partly built then idled; no production reported.

A snippet (Skillings) cites 2025 nickel 28,000 t and a 60,000 t nameplate - not used. Possible overlap with a nickel-commodity Ambatovy row from another slice.

Output is 100% basis of the plant. Product is MHP, so the 'cobalt contained in MHP' is intermediate, not refined cobalt. Possible overlap with a nickel-commodity Ramu row from another slice.

fields.asset_name: Goro (Prony Resources) nickel-cobalt mine and HPAL plant

rows.notes: Mining Technology (undated): Goro designed for 57,000 tpa Ni and 5,000 tpa Co, located in south New Caledonia; monthly target 3,500 t of nickel and cobalt chemicals. Search snippets (not opened): plant restarted 9 Dec 2024 after ~7 months idle; a Mining.com report (dated July 2026 on the page) says output was cut after a tailings dam leak. No 2025 cobalt output found (Mining Data Online lists cobalt 1,703-3,188 t across years, labels garbled). Status operational is therefore weakly evidenced; capacity is design, not actual. [lead] capacity_ref_year = access-year (source undated) fallback.

Glencore FY2025 production report p.12: Murrin Murrin total cobalt metal 2.2 kt own-sourced in 2025 (2.5 kt in 2024); 2.3 kt including third-party feed (2.8 kt in 2024). Own-sourced nickel 32.1 kt. Integrated site (mine + HPAL + refinery) held as one cobalt row; refinery capacity not retrieved. Possible overlap with a nickel-commodity Murrin Murrin row from another slice.

Glencore reports cobalt metal only at the level of 'Integrated Nickel Operations (Sudbury, Raglan, Nikkelverk)': 0.4 kt own-sourced and 3.0 kt including third-party feed in 2025 (3.0 kt in 2024). The refined cobalt is assumed to be made at Nikkelverk (the only refinery in the group), but the report does not state the split, so confidence is limited. Location (Kristiansand, Norway) is general knowledge, not in the cited table. Sudbury and Raglan mines not added as separate cobalt rows (no per-mine data).

fields.product: cobalt concentrate (refined to cathodes at Guemassa)

rows.notes: CONFLICT: Managem product page gives 650 t of cobalt cathodes (as of 31 Dec 2025); Medias24 (reported snippet, page 403) says 507 t of cobalt cathodes in 2025, -61% y/y. Neither is mine output of concentrate; cathodes are made at Guemassa from Bou Azzer concentrate. Managem expects ~2,870 t Co in 2026 once a cobalt sulphate unit starts (snippet; capacity statements conflict: 2,880 t CoSO4 ~590 t Co vs 1,200 t Co metal + 5,800 t sulphate). Bou Azzer described as one of the world's only primary cobalt mines. No coordinates.

Kitco (Mar 2023): Jervois suspended final construction and full concentrator commissioning at its 100%-owned ICO mine in Idaho (low cobalt prices, construction inflation). Search snippets (Idaho DEQ doc, not opened): site moving from short-term suspension to long-term care and maintenance; water treatment to stop from Nov 2025. Jervois recapitalised via Chapter 11 (Millstreet) in 2025 (snippet). Capacity not stated in any fetched page - left null. Status under_construction + paused because it was built but never reached commercial production.

fields.asset_name: Kokkola cobalt refinery and precursor plant (Umicore)
fields.jv_partners: Jervois Finland (toll-refining rights, per search snippet)

rows.notes: Umicore 2019 release (confirmed quote): Europe's largest cobalt refinery, acquired from Freeport Cobalt; Umicore Sept 2020 release (not quoted) says Olen cobalt refining moves to Kokkola by mid-2023. Capacity 15,000 t/y from a Mining Journal search snippet at acquisition time (reported, dated 2020; unit assumed t Co - unverified). I found NO evidence of a 2025/26 sale of Kokkola by Umicore; the lead's 'now Jervois Finland -> sold?' is unresolved: Jervois (via Freeport Cobalt) holds toll-refining rights (~40% of capacity, snippet) and its Chapter 11 recapitalisation was in 2025. No production figure found.

Reported tier only (search-result summaries; the press release page returned 503): initial capacity ~5,120 tpa battery-grade cobalt sulfate rising to ~6,500 tpa; mechanical completion targeted Q2 2027; US$73m construction budget; construction resumed Nov 2025. Location Temiskaming Shores/New Liskeard per search results. Unit assumed CoSO4 as stated ('cobalt sulfate'); hydration state not stated. Publication date of the release not confirmed (null).
